records.claim_text: The Scottish Government annual audit describes an executive Steering Committee and a reporting Programme Management Board, with separate finance-review, vendor, design and customer arrangements; the auditor judged governance appropriate and functioning as expected.
records.locator: Printed/PDF p41, paras117–119 and preceding governance bullets
records.limitations: Membership and supplier attendance do not establish individual vetoes, signature powers or universal organisational design.

records.claim_text: Two HR functional heads signed off moving the HR data-migration process into the live system on 14 August 2024, a narrower decision than the later final programme go-live approval.
records.locator: Printed/PDF p43, para125; compare p46 paras138–140
records.limitations: Do not equate migration-process signoff with all testing acceptance, funding approval or final go-live.

records.claim_text: Programme Management Board recommended1 October 2024 go-live on 19September subject to specified outstanding factors; Steering Committee backed proceeding conditionally on 20September, then formally approved the1 October date on 30September after considering remaining risks and assurances.
records.limitations: One programme; approval with known risks does not establish complete issue closure or universal readiness thresholds.

records.claim_text: The audit records assigned owners for cutover activities and an overall cutover manager, separating execution responsibility from the Steering Committee go-live approval.
records.limitations: Does not identify every contractual acceptance or commercial-signing role.

records.claim_text: The closure account labels external assurance checkpoints separately from internal stage gates and describes a later benefits-management strategy approval. These are distinct events, not evidence that all benefits were realised.
records.locator: Section 6.0 milestone list and Audit Recommendations, recommendation 13 response
records.time_period: Checkpoints 2020–2024; benefits-strategy approval June 2025; published 23 March 2026
records.limitations: Same programme as SRC-0134; management self-review. Checkpoint labels do not disclose every formal decision right.

records.claim_text: Rotherham records an Assistant Chief Executive-delegated award for incumbent iTrent support/maintenance after framework further competition, with Finance, Legal and HR review of a business case signed off by that officer. The stated route preserves an existing platform.
records.locator: Decision Maker, Delegation, Decision, Reasons and Alternatives; page lines29–64
records.time_period: Decision body22 March 2024; published heading 26 March 2024
records.limitations: One council; consultation/review is not a veto. Signature-date line says 2023, retained as inconsistency. Award not proof of later execution/outcomes.

records.claim_text: On8 May 2025 Argyll and Bute Policy and Resources Committee approved continuing Phase2 of an HR/payroll implementation and £480,000 additional 2025/26 resources from part of an earmarked reserve.
records.locator: Item 10, decision points1–2; original minutes lines244–252
records.unit: GBP approved additional budget, not realised spend
records.limitations: Additional-budget approval, not actual expenditure, new contract award, completion, go-live authority or realised return.

records.claim_text: Argyll’s supporting report separates earlier business-case/funding/procurement steps from delivery, identifies a Project Board/SRO and multidisciplinary input, and records Board resource redirection plus ELT prioritisation before the subsequent Committee funding decision.
records.locator: PDF pp2–4, sections2.1,4.2.1–4.2.3; original report lines33–39,99–123
records.time_period: Report for 8 May 2025; earlier 2021–2024 decisions described retrospectively
records.limitations: Same employer/programme as R4CASE-C07, not independent market corroboration. Does not identify final go-live approver; membership does not create individual vetoes.

guardrails: Separate recommendation, conditional approval, budget authority, procurement award, contract execution, functional signoff, go-live and measured result.
No universal CFO veto, private-employer hierarchy, country-wide prevalence, failure rate or ROI is derived.
Missing dates and approval rights stay unknown; no chronology reconstructed from attendance or consultation.
